what: Internalization of the sacrifice: the horse as the cosmos (BAU 1.1), the udgītha as breath (BAU 1.3; ChU 1.1-2), the person as a soma sacrifice (ChU 3.16-17), the inner agnihotra (KauU 2.5), the agnihotra into the breaths (ChU 5.19-24).

evidence.detail: Śāṇḍilya's teaching and the vaiśvānara teaching also appear in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (10.6.3; 10.6.1) (moderate)
the Upaniṣads are transmitted as the final portions (Veda-anta) of the Vedic texts of each śākhā
introduced as verses of the seers ('tad uktam ṛṣiṇā', 'tad eṣa śloko bhavati')

what: Verses and images reused in the Bhagavad Gītā: KU 1.2.18-19 ~ BhG 2.19-20; KU 2.3.1 (inverted aśvattha) ~ BhG 15.1; ŚU 3.16-17 ~ BhG 13.13-14; KU 1.2.15 ~ BhG 8.11 (moderate).

evidence.detail: a later invocation verse calls the Upaniṣads the cows and the Gītā their milk

what: Terms later systematized in Sāṃkhya appear in the Kaṭha (avyakta, mahat, puruṣa in a ladder) and Śvetāśvatara (pradhāna, guṇa, kṣetrajña, 'sāṃkhya-yoga', the seer Kapila).

evidence.detail: the Vedānta tradition (Brahma Sūtra 1.4.1-7) denies that these passages teach Sāṃkhya's pradhāna; Sāṃkhya authors claim śruti support

what: Yoga vocabulary and method in the Upaniṣads — yoga as firm holding of the senses (KU 2.3.11), posture, breath and signs (ŚU 2), the six-limbed yoga (MaiU 6.18) — shared with Patañjala Yoga's limbs (prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā, samādhi).
era: last centuries BCE – early centuries CE

evidence.detail: MaiU 6.18 shares five of its six limbs with YS 2.29

what: The Śvetāśvatara's theology of one Lord named Rudra, Śiva and Hara who frees from fetters (pāśa) by knowledge and grace is cited as śruti by Śaiva authors.

evidence.detail: Rudra, Śiva, Hara, Maheśvara, pāśa, prasāda (ŚU 1.10, 3.2, 3.11, 4.10, 4.16)
Śaiva Siddhānta regards the ŚU as a principal Upaniṣadic authority (moderate)

what: The compound 'prapañcopaśama' with 'śiva' describes the fourth in MāU 7 and the teaching of dependent origination in the dedicatory verse of Nāgārjuna's Mūlamadhyamakakārikā.

evidence.detail: direction of borrowing, if any, is debated; not asserted here
